chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Safwan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Minhal al-Qammat, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Our companions seek the 'Aqeeqa when it is the time of the arrival of the Bedouins, so they find the breeding males; and when it is not that time, they cannot find it, so it becomes heavy/costly upon them.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is merely a sheep of meat, not at the status of the Udhiyah (sacrificial animal of Hajj). Anything suffices from it.'

key_terms.الْأُضْحِيَة: Al-Udhiyah: The sacrificial animal offered during Hajj
key_terms.الْعَقِيقَة: Aqeeqa: Sacrifice made for a newborn child

ai.seo_question: What are the requirements for the animal used in Aqeeqa compared to the Hajj sacrifice?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes the 'Aqeeqa from the Udhiyah by emphasizing its nature as sustenance rather than a strict ritual offering, thereby permitting any sheep regardless of age or quality. This ruling alleviates the economic burden on families, particularly during off-seasons when prime livestock are scarce, reflecting the Shia scholarly view that 'Aqeeqa is a recommended act of gratitude and provision rather than a mandatory condition of validity. The narration underscores the flexibility in Islamic jurisprudence to accommodate practical realities while maintaining the spiritual significance of the sacrifice.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Abbas Bin Marouf, from Safwan, from Abdul Rahman Bin Al Hajjaj, from Minhal Al Qammat who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘Our companions are seeking the Aqeeqa when the Bedouins come over, so they are finding the stallions; and when it is other than that they cannot find it, and it is a (heavy) cost upon them’. So heasws said: ‘But rather, it is a sheep, flesh which is not at the status of the sacrificial animal (during Hajj). Everything suffices from it’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-‘ Abbas ibn M‘aruf from Safwan ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn al- Hajj a] from Minhal al-Qammat who has said the following: “Once

I said to abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, that our people can find animals for ‘Aqiqah when Arabs are around. They can find ram but in other seasons such an animal is difficult to find and it is expensive for them. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is only a sheep and it is not like the sacrificial offering for al-Hajj. Anything is sufficient for it.’”
